notes.editorial_method: All 86 source paragraphs in Sections A and B were manually rewritten in both English and bilingual Telugu. English legal and scientific terms are retained inside simple Telugu narration; no source paragraph was retained verbatim.
factual_corrections: BDA 2023 Amendment provisions discussed here commenced on 1 April 2024; describing the new section 37 procedure merely as a 2023 procedure omits its effective date.
SBB treatment of section 7 Indian access is based on prior intimation and sections 23–24 powers, not a universal prior-approval model.

BDA penalties: ₹1–50 lakh is the ordinary range under the 2024 Rules; damage may justify a commensurate amount, and failure or continued contravention can attract an additional penalty up to ₹1 crore. Repeated violation is not the precise Gazette wording.
The cultivated-medicinal-plant and codified-knowledge exclusions are conditional and actor-specific, not a blanket AYUSH exemption.
Biological Diversity Rules, 2024: signed 22 October, Gazette-published 25 October, commenced 24 December 2024.

source_metadata_suggestions.use_for: Schedules, hunting, protected areas, section 62, tiger reserves and 2022 amendment commencement

Gazette of India — Biological Diversity Rules, 2024, G.S.R. 665(E)

source_concerns: Live-dashboard totals dated September 2026 should retain an archived capture or dated official export before publication because live totals can change.
Statements describing government benefits or critics' concerns about the 2023 Amendment are policy assessments, not statutory text, and should remain explicitly attributed.
ESZ application depends on the site notification and Supreme Court orders; avoid presenting one nationwide fixed-width rule.

paragraphs.en: Wildlife and habitats in India are protected through several laws, not a single statute. The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 (WPA) protects wild species and creates protected-area categories. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 (EPA) provides regulatory tools such as Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs) and Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA). Both laws may apply to the same landscape, but their legal functions are different.
paragraphs.te: Indiaలో wildlife, habitats రక్షణ ఒకే lawతో జరగదు. Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 (WPA) wild speciesను protect చేసి, protected-area categoriesను ఏర్పాటు చేస్తుంది. Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 (EPA) కింద Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs), Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) వంటి regulatory tools పనిచేస్తాయి. ఒకే landscapeకు రెండు laws వర్తించవచ్చు; కానీ వాటి legal functions వేర్వేరు.

paragraphs.en: The WPA is India's principal wildlife-protection law. It prohibits or regulates hunting and trade in wild animals, specified plants and their derivatives, and it authorises governments to notify protected areas. The original six schedules were reorganised by the 2022 Amendment. In each state, the Chief Wildlife Warden is the principal officer responsible for implementing the Act.
paragraphs.te: WPA అనేది Indiaలో ప్రధాన wildlife-protection law. Wild animals, specified plants, వాటి derivativesకు సంబంధించిన hunting, tradeను ఇది prohibit లేదా regulate చేస్తుంది. Protected areasను notify చేసే authorityని కూడా governmentsకు ఇస్తుంది. మొదట ఉన్న six Schedulesను 2022 Amendment reorganise చేసింది. State levelలో Act implementationకు Chief Wildlife Warden ప్రధాన officer.

paragraphs.en: The WPA was enacted against the background of serious wildlife decline after Independence. It later became the statutory foundation for recovery programmes such as Project Tiger. Parliament created the national framework, while designated state authorities carry out much of the field administration, permissions and wildlife control.
paragraphs.te: Independence తరువాత wildlife populations తీవ్రంగా తగ్గుతున్న సమయంలో WPA వచ్చింది. తరువాత Project Tiger వంటి recovery programmesకు ఇది statutory foundation అయింది. Parliament national legal frameworkను రూపొందించింది; field administration, statutory permissions, wildlife controlలో ఎక్కువ పని designated State authorities నిర్వహిస్తాయి.

paragraphs.en: The Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 came into force on 1 April 2023. It reduced the earlier six schedules to four, created an explicit framework for implementing CITES, authorised regulation of invasive alien species, widened the provision for Conservation Reserves and permitted voluntary surrender of specified captive animals or articles without compensation.
paragraphs.te: Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 provisions 1 April 2023 నుంచి అమల్లోకి వచ్చాయి. Earlier six Schedulesను four Schedulesగా మార్చింది. CITES implementationకు explicit frameworkను ఇచ్చింది; invasive alien speciesను regulate చేసే powerను చేర్చింది; Conservation Reserves scopeను విస్తరించింది. Specified captive animals లేదా articlesను compensation లేకుండా voluntarily surrender చేసే provisionను కూడా ఇచ్చింది.

paragraphs.en: Section 9 generally prohibits hunting animals listed in Schedules I and II. In the Act, hunting includes killing, poisoning, capturing or trapping an animal, injuring it, and attempting these acts; it also covers specified damage to bird or reptile eggs and nests. Exceptions are limited and must fit provisions such as sections 11 and 12. Killing or wounding an animal in good-faith defence of oneself or another person is not an offence, but that defence cannot be used to justify a prior illegal act.
paragraphs.te: Section 9 ప్రకారం Schedules I, IIలో ఉన్న animalsను hunting చేయడం సాధారణంగా prohibited. Actలో hunting అంటే killing మాత్రమే కాదు; poisoning, capturing, trapping, injuring, వాటికి attempt చేయడం కూడా. Birds లేదా reptiles eggs, nestsకు Actలో చెప్పిన damage కూడా ఇందులోకి రావచ్చు. Exceptions sections 11, 12 వంటి provisionsలో ఉన్న limited casesకే వర్తిస్తాయి. తనను లేదా మరో personను రక్షించడానికి good faithలో animalను kill లేదా wound చేస్తే offence కాదు; కానీ ముందుగా చేసిన illegal actను సమర్థించడానికి self-defenceను ఉపయోగించలేరు.

paragraphs.en: The deletion of old Schedule V did not abolish the vermin power. Under section 62, only the Central Government may notify a Schedule II animal as vermin for a specified area and period. Schedule I animals are excluded. Once the notification ends, the animal again receives the Act's ordinary protection.
paragraphs.te: Old Schedule Vను delete చేసినా vermin power రద్దు కాలేదు. Section 62 కింద Schedule II animalను specified area, specified period కోసం verminగా notify చేయగల authority Central Governmentకే ఉంది. Schedule I animalsకు ఈ provision వర్తించదు. Notification period ముగిసిన తరువాత ఆ animalకు Actలోని normal protection మళ్లీ వర్తిస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries are statutory protected areas under the WPA, but the treatment of existing rights is not identical. A Conservation Reserve generally covers government-owned land adjoining or linking protected areas, after consultation with local communities. A Community Reserve is declared over private or community land whose owners volunteer it for wildlife and habitat conservation; ownership does not pass to the government merely because the reserve is notified.
paragraphs.te: National Park, Wildlife Sanctuary రెండూ WPA కింద statutory protected areas. కానీ existing rightsను deal చేసే విధానం రెండింటిలో identical కాదు. Conservation Reserve సాధారణంగా protected areasకు adjoiningగా లేదా ecological linkగా ఉన్న government-owned landపై, local communitiesతో consultation తరువాత ఏర్పడుతుంది. Community Reserve కోసం private లేదా community land owners స్వచ్ఛందంగా landను conservationకు offer చేస్తారు. Reserve notify అయినంత మాత్రాన ownership governmentకు transfer కాదు.

paragraphs.en: An Eco-Sensitive Zone around a protected area is notified under section 3 of the EPA and the Environment (Protection) Rules; it is not a WPA protected-area category. Its extent and activity restrictions are site-specific. Ten kilometres is therefore not a compulsory width for every ESZ. The Supreme Court's 2022 and modified 2023 directions must be read with the draft or final notification applicable to the particular protected area.
paragraphs.te: Protected area చుట్టూ Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ)ను EPA section 3, Environment (Protection) Rules కింద notify చేస్తారు. ESZ అనేది WPA protected-area category కాదు. దాని extent, activity restrictions site-specificగా ఉంటాయి; అందుకే ప్రతి ESZకు 10 kilometres compulsory width కాదు. Particular protected areaకు వర్తించే draft లేదా final notificationతో పాటు Supreme Court 2022 directions, 2023 modificationను కలిపి చదవాలి.

paragraphs.en: Tiger Reserves, Elephant Reserves and Biosphere Reserves do not have the same legal status. A Tiger Reserve has a statutory basis in Chapter IV-B of the WPA and may overlap a National Park or Sanctuary. An Elephant Reserve is an administrative recognition under Project Elephant, not a separate statutory land category. A Biosphere Reserve is designated nationally under the Man and the Biosphere framework; later inclusion in UNESCO's World Network is a separate international recognition. Enforceable restrictions in its core arise from the underlying National Park, Sanctuary or forest-law status, not from the Biosphere Reserve label alone.
paragraphs.te: Tiger Reserve, Elephant Reserve, Biosphere Reserveకు same legal status ఉండదు. Tiger Reserveకు WPA Chapter IV-B కింద statutory basis ఉంది; అది National Park లేదా Sanctuaryతో overlap కావచ్చు. Elephant Reserve అనేది Project Elephant కింద administrative recognition; separate statutory land category కాదు. Biosphere Reserveను national levelలో Man and the Biosphere framework కింద designate చేస్తారు; UNESCO World Networkలో inclusion అనేది separate international recognition. Core areaలో enforceable restrictions, Biosphere Reserve label వల్ల alone రావు; underlying National Park, Sanctuary లేదా forest-law status నుంచి వస్తాయి.

paragraphs.en: Ramsar status comes from the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands, an international treaty adopted in 1971, not from an Indian protected-area law. India nominates a qualifying wetland and it is added to the international List after the Convention process is completed. Domestic restrictions arise through Indian law, including the Wetlands Rules, 2017, and not from the Ramsar label alone. Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park, designated on 1 October 1981, were India's first Ramsar Sites. Keoladeo shows that the same place may be both a Ramsar Site and a WPA protected area.
paragraphs.te: Ramsar status, 1971 Ramsar Convention on Wetlands అనే international treaty నుంచి వస్తుంది; Indian protected-area law నుంచి కాదు. India qualifying wetlandను nominate చేస్తుంది; Convention process పూర్తయ్యాక అది international Listలో చేరుతుంది. Domestic restrictions Ramsar label alone వల్ల రావు; Wetlands Rules, 2017 వంటి Indian laws ద్వారా వస్తాయి. 1 October 1981న designate అయిన Chilika Lake, Keoladeo National Park India first Ramsar Sites. Keoladeo ఒకే placeకు Ramsar status, WPA protected-area status రెండూ ఉండవచ్చని చూపుతుంది.

paragraphs.en: The Central Government, acting through MoEFCC and generally on a state proposal, notifies an ESZ under sections 3(1) and 3(2)(v) of the EPA and the related Rules. The site notification specifies its boundary and classifies activities as prohibited, regulated or permissible. Thus an ESZ is an EPA regulatory buffer, not an additional National Park or Sanctuary.
paragraphs.te: సాధారణంగా State proposal ఆధారంగా Central Government, MoEFCC ద్వారా, EPA sections 3(1), 3(2)(v), related Rules కింద ESZను notify చేస్తుంది. Site notification boundaryని నిర్ణయించి, activitiesను prohibited, regulated లేదా permissibleగా classify చేస్తుంది. కాబట్టి ESZ అనేది EPA regulatory buffer; additional National Park లేదా Sanctuary కాదు.

paragraphs.en: Section 37 of the Biological Diversity Act creates the Biodiversity Heritage Site (BHS) designation. The procedure substituted by the 2023 Amendment came into force on 1 April 2024. The State Biodiversity Board must first consult the local body and the Biodiversity Management Committee and then recommend the site. Only the State Government issues the Gazette notification.
paragraphs.te: Biological Diversity Act section 37, Biodiversity Heritage Site (BHS) designationను create చేస్తుంది. 2023 Amendment substitute చేసిన procedure 1 April 2024 నుంచి అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది. State Biodiversity Board ముందుగా local body, Biodiversity Management Committeeతో consult చేసి, siteను recommend చేయాలి. Gazette notificationను State Government మాత్రమే issue చేస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: An Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measure (OECM) recognises effective, long-term area-based conservation outside the formal protected-area system. It is a CBD reporting category, not a statutory designation created by the WPA or BDA. India's framework groups possible OECMs into fourteen categories, and qualifying areas may be identified voluntarily for national compilation and CBD reporting. Recognition alone does not create a new binding legal or financial protection. Eligible OECMs can contribute to KMGBF Target 3.
paragraphs.te: Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measure (OECM) అంటే formal protected-area system బయట long-term area-based conservation effectiveగా జరుగుతున్న placeకు ఇచ్చే recognition. ఇది CBD reporting category; WPA లేదా BDA create చేసిన statutory designation కాదు. India frameworkలో possible OECMsను fourteen categoriesగా group చేశారు. Qualifying areasను voluntarily identify చేసి national compilation, CBD reportingలో include చేయవచ్చు. Recognition alone కొత్త binding legal లేదా financial protectionను create చేయదు. Eligible OECMs, KMGBF Target 3కు contribute చేయగలవు.

paragraphs.en: Marine Protected Area is a descriptive expression in India, not a separate protected-area category under the WPA. A marine site receives enforceable protection through an underlying legal designation such as a National Park or Wildlife Sanctuary. The legal label identifies the applicable statute; conservation effectiveness depends on implementation in the field.
paragraphs.te: Indiaలో Marine Protected Area (MPA) అనేది descriptive term; WPAలో separate protected-area category కాదు. Marine siteకు enforceable protection, National Park లేదా Wildlife Sanctuary వంటి underlying legal designation నుంచి వస్తుంది. Legal label ఏ statute వర్తిస్తుందో చెబుతుంది; conservation ఎంత effectiveగా ఉందో field implementation నిర్ణయిస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: A Tiger Reserve is an additional statutory layer under Chapter IV-B of the WPA, often placed over land that already has protected status. Altering the boundary of a National Park or Sanctuary requires a recommendation of the National Board for Wild Life. A Tiger Reserve boundary alteration additionally requires recommendations of both the National Tiger Conservation Authority and the National Board for Wild Life. De-notification also requires a finding that it is in the public interest and approval of the National Board for Wild Life.
paragraphs.te: Tiger Reserve అనేది WPA Chapter IV-B కింద additional statutory layer; already protected status ఉన్న landపై కూడా ఇది ఉండవచ్చు. National Park లేదా Sanctuary boundary alterationకు National Board for Wild Life recommendation అవసరం. Tiger Reserve boundary alterationకు National Tiger Conservation Authority, National Board for Wild Life రెండింటి recommendations అవసరం. De-notification కోసం change public interestలో ఉందనే findingతో పాటు National Board for Wild Life approval కూడా కావాలి.

topic_group.en: Biological Diversity Act and local institutions
topic_group.te: జీవ వైవిధ్య చట్టం మరియు స్థానిక సంస్థలు

title.en: Biological Diversity Act and local institutions
title.te: జీవ వైవిధ్య చట్టం మరియు స్థానిక సంస్థలు

paragraphs.en: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (BDA) governs access to India's biological resources and the fair sharing of benefits obtained from their use, a system known as Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS). It distributes these responsibilities among the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and local Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs). The clearest way to tell the three apart is to ask who creates each body and what duty the Act assigns to it.
paragraphs.te: Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (BDA), Indiaలోని biological resourcesను ఎవరు access చేయవచ్చు, వాటి use వల్ల వచ్చే benefitsను ఎలా న్యాయంగా పంచాలి అనే విషయాలను నియంత్రిస్తుంది. ఈ విధానాన్నే Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) అంటారు. దీనికి సంబంధించిన బాధ్యతలను Act మూడు bodiesకు పంచింది: National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs), local Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs). వీటి మధ్య తేడా తెలుసుకోవాలంటే ఒక్కో bodyని ఎవరు ఏర్పాటు చేస్తారు, దానికి Act ఏ పని అప్పగించింది అనే రెండు విషయాలు చూడాలి.

paragraphs.en: India adopted the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 to give domestic effect to its commitments under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). The Act places two linked ideas at its centre: regulating access to biological resources and sharing the resulting benefits fairly and equitably. Its institutions operate at national, state and local-government levels, connecting national regulation with biological resources and knowledge held by local communities.
paragraphs.te: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) కింద India అంగీకరించిన commitmentsను దేశంలో అమలు చేయడానికి Biological Diversity Act, 2002 వచ్చింది. Biological resourcesకు accessను regulate చేయడం, వాటి use వల్ల వచ్చే benefitsను fair and equitableగా పంచడం—ఇవి Actలోని రెండు ప్రధాన అంశాలు. National, State, local-government levelsలో పనిచేసే institutions ద్వారా national regulationకు local biological resources, community knowledgeతో సంబంధం ఏర్పడుతుంది.

paragraphs.en: India ratified the CBD in 1994, whereas the BDA was enacted in 2002. In the intervening period, foreign patent claims concerning turmeric's wound-healing use, neem's pesticidal properties, and the name or characteristics of basmati rice became prominent biopiracy disputes. India challenged these claims through legal and diplomatic routes, with complete or partial success. Because India then lacked a domestic ABS law capable of addressing such claims at the outset, the disputes strengthened the case for national legislation.
paragraphs.te: India 1994లో CBDని ratify చేసింది; BDA మాత్రం 2002లో enact అయింది. ఈ మధ్యకాలంలో turmeric wound-healing use, neem pesticidal properties, basmati rice పేరు లేదా లక్షణాలకు సంబంధించిన foreign patent claims ప్రముఖ biopiracy disputesగా మారాయి. India వాటిని legal, diplomatic routesలో challenge చేసి పూర్తిగా లేదా కొంతవరకు విజయం సాధించింది. ఇటువంటి claimsను మొదటి దశలోనే address చేసే domestic ABS law అప్పటికి లేకపోవడంతో national legislation అవసరం మరింత బలంగా కనిపించింది.

paragraphs.en: The National Biodiversity Authority is the national-level body and has its headquarters in Chennai. It regulates access to Indian biological resources and associated knowledge by the foreign-linked persons and entities identified in the Act. It also determines or oversees benefit-sharing arrangements and advises the Central Government on biodiversity-related matters.
paragraphs.te: National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) national levelలో పనిచేస్తుంది; దీని headquarters Chennaiలో ఉంది. Act పేర్కొన్న foreign-linked persons, entities Indian biological resources లేదా వాటికి సంబంధించిన knowledgeను access చేసే విధానాన్ని NBA regulate చేస్తుంది. Benefit-sharing arrangementsను నిర్ణయించడం లేదా పర్యవేక్షించడం, biodiversity mattersపై Central Governmentకు advice ఇవ్వడం కూడా దీని బాధ్యతలు.

paragraphs.en: A State Biodiversity Board functions at the state level. Sections 23 and 24 require it to advise the State Government and deal with prior intimations submitted by Indian persons covered by section 7. If an inquiry establishes the grounds specified in the Act, the Board may prohibit or restrict the activity. Its role should not be reduced to 'prior approval', because the statutory process is based on prior intimation and the Board's inquiry powers.
paragraphs.te: State Biodiversity Board (SBB) State levelలో పనిచేస్తుంది. Sections 23, 24 ప్రకారం ఇది State Governmentకు advice ఇస్తుంది; section 7 పరిధిలోని Indian persons సమర్పించే prior intimationsను పరిశీలిస్తుంది. Actలో చెప్పిన grounds ఉన్నాయని inquiryలో తేలితే, ఆ activityని prohibit లేదా restrict చేయవచ్చు. కాబట్టి SBB roleను కేవలం ‘prior approval’గా చెప్పడం సరికాదు; ఇక్కడ process prior intimation, inquiry powersపై ఆధారపడి ఉంటుంది.

paragraphs.en: Every rural and urban local body must constitute a Biodiversity Management Committee. The BMC prepares a People's Biodiversity Register (PBR) to record the biological resources and associated traditional knowledge found within its jurisdiction. A PBR is therefore not merely a species checklist: it can document a community's contribution and later support its claim to benefit sharing.
paragraphs.te: ప్రతి rural, urban local body ఒక Biodiversity Management Committee (BMC)ని ఏర్పాటు చేయాలి. తన jurisdictionలో ఉన్న biological resources, వాటికి సంబంధించిన traditional knowledgeను BMC, People's Biodiversity Register (PBR)లో నమోదు చేస్తుంది. అందువల్ల PBR కేవలం species list కాదు. అది local community contributionను document చేసి, తరువాత benefit-sharing claimకు ఆధారంగా ఉపయోగపడుతుంది.

paragraphs.en: If a biological resource or traditional knowledge is later put to commercial use, the PBR can help trace its place and community of origin. Using that record, the BMC can support the community's claim for compensation or a share of the benefits. When reliable documentation is absent, proving an entitlement under the Act's ABS provisions becomes considerably harder.
paragraphs.te: ఒక biological resource లేదా traditional knowledge తరువాత commercial useలోకి వెళితే, అది ఏ ప్రాంతం లేదా community నుంచి వచ్చిందో PBR ద్వారా trace చేయవచ్చు. ఆ recordను ఉపయోగించి BMC, communityకి compensation లేదా benefit share రావాలనే claimకు మద్దతు ఇవ్వగలదు. Reliable documentation లేకపోతే Actలోని ABS provisions కింద entitlementను prove చేయడం చాలా కష్టమవుతుంది.

paragraphs.en: The BMC–PBR network is India's local institutional foundation for documenting biological resources and supporting ABS under the BDA. The Cali Fund belongs to a different system: it is a CBD multilateral mechanism for benefits from the commercial use of digital sequence information. Its principle that at least half of disbursements should reach Indigenous peoples and local communities is not a rule of the BMC–PBR framework. National counts of BMCs and PBRs instead indicate how widely India's statutory local tier has become operational.
paragraphs.te: BDA కింద biological resourcesను local levelలో document చేయడానికి, ABSకు support ఇవ్వడానికి BMC–PBR network పునాదిగా పనిచేస్తుంది. Cali Fund దీనికి వేరైన mechanism. Digital sequence information commercial use నుంచి వచ్చే benefits కోసం CBD కింద ఇది multilateral mechanismగా ఏర్పడింది. Fund disbursementsలో కనీసం 50% Indigenous peoples, local communitiesకు ఇవ్వాలనే principle, BMC–PBR frameworkలోని rule కాదు. BMCలు, PBRల national counts మాత్రం India statutory local tier ఎంత విస్తృతంగా operational అయిందో చూపిస్తాయి.

paragraphs.en: The NBA live dashboard showed 2,76,664 constituted BMCs and 2,72,648 prepared PBRs in India by September 2026. These are administrative totals recorded on a particular date, not permanent figures. Viewed together, they show both the geographical spread of the local system and how many constituted committees had produced a biodiversity register by then.
paragraphs.te: NBA live dashboard ప్రకారం September 2026 నాటికి Indiaలో 2,76,664 BMCs ఏర్పాటు అయ్యాయి; 2,72,648 PBRs సిద్ధమయ్యాయి. ఇవి permanent figures కావు; ఒక particular dateకు చెందిన administrative totals. ఈ రెండు numbersను కలిపి చూస్తే local system geographical spread ఎంత ఉందో, ఏర్పాటు అయిన committeesలో ఎన్ని అప్పటికి biodiversity registerను సిద్ధం చేశాయో తెలుస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: By institutional count, the BMC tier—with more than 2.5 lakh committees—is India's largest conservation-governance network. Its number is far above the approximately 1,014 protected areas discussed later in this lesson. This is only a comparison of scale: a local committee and a legally protected geographical area differ in both purpose and legal character.
paragraphs.te: 2.5 లక్షలకు పైగా committees ఉన్నందున, institutional countలో BMC tier Indiaలో largest conservation-governance network. ఈ Lessonలో తరువాత వచ్చే సుమారు 1,014 protected areas countతో పోలిస్తే ఇది చాలా పెద్ద సంఖ్య. కానీ ఇది scale comparison మాత్రమే. Local committee, legally protected geographical area—వాటి purpose, legal character రెండూ వేర్వేరు.

paragraphs.en: The PBR total trails the BMC total by only about four thousand. This close numerical match suggests that most constituted committees were followed by preparation of a local biodiversity register. It points to broad availability of the documentary base needed for benefit-sharing claims, but the numbers alone cannot establish the quality of each PBR.
paragraphs.te: BMC totalతో పోలిస్తే PBR total సుమారు 4,000 మాత్రమే తక్కువ. ఈ రెండు numbers దగ్గరగా ఉండటం వల్ల, చాలా చోట్ల committee ఏర్పడిన తరువాత local biodiversity register కూడా సిద్ధమైందని అర్థమవుతుంది. Benefit-sharing claimsకు అవసరమైన documentary base విస్తృతంగా ఉందని ఇది సూచిస్తుంది. అయితే numbers మాత్రమే ప్రతి PBR qualityని నిర్ధారించలేవు.

paragraphs.en: Wide numerical coverage does not automatically mean high-quality documentation. A PBR may be officially completed but still contain gaps, poorly verified scientific information or entries that are no longer current. The near-equal BMC and PBR totals demonstrate administrative reach; completeness and present accuracy can be judged only by examining the registers themselves.
paragraphs.te: ఎక్కువ సంఖ్యలో PBRs ఉండటం అంటే వాటి documentation quality కూడా తప్పకుండా బాగుందని కాదు. ఒక PBR officially complete అయినప్పటికీ, అందులో gaps ఉండవచ్చు; scientific informationకు సరైన verification లేకపోవచ్చు; entries outdated అయి ఉండవచ్చు. BMC, PBR totals దగ్గరగా ఉండటం administrative reachను చూపుతుంది. Completeness, current accuracy తెలుసుకోవాలంటే registersను స్వయంగా examine చేయాలి.

paragraphs.en: BMC and PBR counts help measure how far India's ABS system has extended to the local level. Because these are date-specific administrative figures rather than timeless facts, they must always be read with their reference date. The September 2026 totals describe implementation only as it stood at that time.
paragraphs.te: India ABS system local levelకు ఎంతవరకు చేరిందో అంచనా వేయడానికి BMC, PBR counts ఉపయోగపడతాయి. ఇవి timeless facts కాకుండా date-specific administrative figures కాబట్టి reference dateతో కలిపే చదవాలి. September 2026 totals, ఆ సమయానికి implementation ఎంతవరకు జరిగిందో మాత్రమే తెలియజేస్తాయి.

paragraphs.en: The provision that substituted section 37 through the 2023 Amendment took effect on 1 April 2024. Before proposing a Biodiversity Heritage Site, the SBB must consult the local body and BMC concerned. It then sends its recommendation to the State Government, which alone has the authority to issue the notification.
paragraphs.te: 2023 Amendment ద్వారా substitute చేసిన section 37 provision, 1 April 2024 నుంచి అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది. Biodiversity Heritage Siteను propose చేయడానికి ముందు SBB, concerned local bodyతోను BMCతోను consult చేయాలి. తరువాత తన recommendationను State Governmentకు పంపుతుంది; notification issue చేసే authority State Governmentకే ఉంటుంది.

paragraphs.en: Section 37 adds a place-based conservation mechanism—the Biodiversity Heritage Site—to the NBA–SBB–BMC institutional framework. A site may merit recognition because of exceptional species richness, endemism, rare or threatened species, or cultural heritage closely linked to biodiversity. Thus a sacred grove or a landscape conserving a traditional crop landrace may qualify where ecological and cultural values are preserved together.
paragraphs.te: NBA–SBB–BMC institutional frameworkకు section 37 ఒక place-based conservation mechanismను జోడిస్తుంది; అదే Biodiversity Heritage Site (BHS). Exceptional species richness, endemism, rare లేదా threatened species, biodiversityతో దగ్గరగా ముడిపడిన cultural heritage వంటి విలువల వల్ల ఒక siteకు recognition రావచ్చు. అందుకే sacred grove లేదా traditional crop landraceను కాపాడే landscapeలో ecological, cultural values రెండూ ఉంటే అది qualify కావచ్చు.

paragraphs.en: Formal power to notify a Biodiversity Heritage Site belongs only to the State Government. The 2023 Amendment, however, replaced section 37(1) and altered the procedure that must occur before notification. Since older study material may still describe the earlier process, examination answers should follow the current statutory text.
paragraphs.te: Biodiversity Heritage Siteను formally notify చేసే power State Governmentకు మాత్రమే ఉంది. అయితే 2023 Amendment, section 37(1)ను replace చేసి notificationకు ముందు పాటించాల్సిన procedureను మార్చింది. Older study materialలో పాత process కనిపించవచ్చు. Exam answer మాత్రం current statutory text ప్రకారమే ఉండాలి.

paragraphs.en: Amended section 37 assigns three separate legal functions to different actors. The local body and BMC are consulted; the SBB considers that consultation and recommends the site; the State Government issues the Gazette notification. Consultation, recommendation and notification should therefore never be treated as interchangeable steps.
paragraphs.te: Amended section 37 మూడు separate legal functionsను వేర్వేరు actorsకు ఇచ్చింది. Local body, BMCతో consultation జరుగుతుంది; దాన్ని పరిగణనలోకి తీసుకుని SBB siteను recommend చేస్తుంది; State Government Gazette notificationను issue చేస్తుంది. కాబట్టి consultation, recommendation, notificationను ఒకే stepగా భావించకూడదు.

paragraphs.en: An SBB recommendation is now a compulsory legal condition for notification. The State Government cannot complete a BHS notification without that recommendation. The proviso also gives the BMC an express role: before recommending the site, the SBB must consult both the relevant local body and the BMC.
paragraphs.te: BHS notificationకు SBB recommendation ఇప్పుడు compulsory legal condition. ఆ recommendation లేకుండా State Government notificationను complete చేయలేదు. Proviso, BMCకి కూడా express role ఇచ్చింది. Siteను recommend చేసే ముందు SBB, relevant local bodyతో పాటు BMCతో కూడా తప్పనిసరిగా consult చేయాలి.

paragraphs.en: The State Government retains the final notifying authority. The SBB may recommend and the BMC must be consulted, but neither can issue the BHS notification. In practice, the People's Biodiversity Register maintained by the BMC can supply local evidence of a site's biodiversity value and support its consideration by higher-level bodies.
paragraphs.te: Final notification authority State Governmentకే ఉంటుంది. SBB recommend చేస్తుంది; BMCతో consultation జరుగుతుంది; కానీ ఈ రెండింటిలో ఏ body కూడా BHS notificationను issue చేయలేదు. Practicalగా, BMC maintain చేసే People's Biodiversity Register site biodiversity valueకు local evidenceను అందించి, higher-level considerationకు support ఇవ్వగలదు.

paragraphs.en: In September 2026, the NBA live dashboard listed 57 notified Biodiversity Heritage Sites. The WII–ENVIS database had listed 54 sites in 17 states in January 2024, while still older material reported 44. These figures are not mutually inconsistent: each is a dated snapshot of a network that expands whenever another site is notified.
paragraphs.te: NBA live dashboardలో September 2026 నాటికి 57 notified Biodiversity Heritage Sites కనిపించాయి. WII–ENVIS database January 2024 నాటికి 17 Statesలో 54 sitesను చూపింది; మరింత పాత materialలో 44 అనే figure ఉంది. ఇవి పరస్పరం conflict అయ్యే totals కావు. కొత్త sites notify అవుతున్నకొద్దీ పెరిగే networkకు సంబంధించిన different dated snapshots.

paragraphs.en: The national BHS total changes each time a State Government notifies a new site. More broadly, the BDA places the NBA at national level, SBBs at state level and BMCs at local-body level. Calling this arrangement a three-tier system refers to coordination across levels, not an administrative chain of command. A BMC is constituted by its local body; it is not an SBB field office.
paragraphs.te: State Government కొత్త siteను notify చేసినప్పుడల్లా national BHS total మారుతుంది. BDA structureలో national levelలో NBA, State levelలో SBBs, local-body levelలో BMCs ఉంటాయి. దీనిని three-tier system అనడం levels మధ్య coordinationను సూచిస్తుంది; administrative chain of commandను కాదు. BMCని దాని local body ఏర్పాటు చేస్తుంది; అది SBB field office కాదు.

paragraphs.en: Under amended section 41(1), responsibility for constituting a BMC rests with the local body itself. In a rural area, this is the Gram Panchayat; in an urban area, it is the specified Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Committee or Municipal Corporation. The SBB neither creates the BMC nor appoints or removes its members.
paragraphs.te: Amended section 41(1) ప్రకారం BMCని constitute చేసే బాధ్యత local bodyకే ఉంది. Rural areaలో Gram Panchayat; urban areaలో specified Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Committee లేదా Municipal Corporation ఈ పని చేస్తాయి. SBB, BMCని create చేయదు; దాని membersను appoint చేయదు లేదా remove చేయదు.

paragraphs.en: Each of the three institutions is created by a different authority. Section 8 empowers the Central Government to establish the NBA; section 22 assigns establishment of an SBB to the State Government; and section 41 requires the local body to constitute its BMC. None is merely a branch office of the body placed above it in the three-level arrangement.
paragraphs.te: ఈ మూడు institutionsను different authorities ఏర్పాటు చేస్తాయి. Section 8 కింద Central Government NBAను establish చేస్తుంది; section 22 కింద State Government SBBను establish చేస్తుంది; section 41 కింద local body తన BMCని constitute చేస్తుంది. Three-level arrangementలో ఒక body, దాని పై level bodyకి mere branch office కాదు.

paragraphs.en: A BMC is accountable chiefly within its local-government framework, not through a departmental hierarchy leading to the SBB. The PBR is a local record maintained by the committee, not a routine return submitted to the Board. Section 37 further confirms this distinct local role by requiring the SBB to consult the BMC before it recommends a BHS.
paragraphs.te: BMC ప్రధానంగా తన local-government frameworkలో accountableగా ఉంటుంది; SBBకు వెళ్లే departmental hierarchyలో కాదు. PBR అనేది committee maintain చేసే local record; Boardకు పంపే routine return కాదు. BHS recommendationకు ముందు SBB, BMCతో consult చేయాలని section 37 చెప్పడం కూడా BMC distinct local roleను confirm చేస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: It is wrong to call BMCs the field units of SBBs or to claim that an SBB creates village-level committees. The Central Government establishes the NBA, the State Government establishes the SBB, and the relevant local body constitutes the BMC.
paragraphs.te: BMCలను SBB field unitsగా చెప్పడం, village-level BMCలను SBB ఏర్పాటు చేస్తుందని చెప్పడం తప్పు. Central Government NBAను establish చేస్తుంది; State Government SBBను establish చేస్తుంది; relevant local body BMCని constitute చేస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: The 2023 Amendment, effective from 1 April 2024, replaced criminal punishment for the relevant BDA contraventions with monetary penalties imposed through adjudication. The ordinary range under the 2024 Rules is ₹1 lakh to ₹50 lakh. Where assessed damage is higher, the penalty may be fixed at a commensurate amount; failure or a continuing contravention can attract an additional penalty of up to ₹1 crore. Any liability arising under another applicable law remains unaffected.
paragraphs.te: 1 April 2024 నుంచి effective అయిన 2023 Amendment, relevant BDA contraventionsకు ఉన్న criminal punishment స్థానంలో adjudication ద్వారా monetary penaltiesను తీసుకొచ్చింది. 2024 Rules కింద ordinary penalty range ₹1 lakh నుంచి ₹50 lakh. Assessed damage దీనికంటే ఎక్కువైతే, damageకు commensurate amountను penaltyగా నిర్ణయించవచ్చు. Failure లేదా continuing contraventionకు additional penalty ₹1 crore వరకు ఉండవచ్చు. మరో applicable law కింద వచ్చే liability మాత్రం అలాగే కొనసాగుతుంది.

paragraphs.en: The exclusions must be read narrowly from amended section 7. They cover codified traditional knowledge; cultivated medicinal plants and their products; specified local people and communities; growers and cultivators; and vaids, hakims and registered AYUSH practitioners who practise indigenous medicine for sustenance and livelihood. They do not create a blanket exemption for every AYUSH enterprise, use of wild biological resources or foreign-linked person. Amended section 6 separately moves the relevant IP trigger from filing an application to grant of the right.
paragraphs.te: Amended section 7లోని exclusionsను narrowగానే చదవాలి. Codified traditional knowledge; cultivated medicinal plants, వాటి products; specified local people, communities; growers, cultivators; sustenance, livelihood కోసం indigenous medicine practice చేసే vaids, hakims, registered AYUSH practitioners వీటి పరిధిలోకి వస్తారు. కానీ every AYUSH enterprise, wild biological resources use లేదా foreign-linked personకు blanket exemption లేదు. వేరుగా, amended section 6లో relevant IP trigger application filing నుంచి right grant దశకు మారింది.

paragraphs.en: Under substituted section 6, the decisive stage is grant of the IP right rather than filing of the application. This change in timing applies to both Indian and foreign applicants. Their legal routes still differ, because each category must fulfil a different obligation at or before that stage.
paragraphs.te: Substituted section 6 ప్రకారం decisive stage IP application filing కాదు; IP right grant. ఈ timing change Indian, foreign applicants ఇద్దరికీ వర్తిస్తుంది. అయినప్పటికీ వారి legal routes వేరు, ఎందుకంటే ఆ stageలో లేదా దానికి ముందు ప్రతి category fulfil చేయాల్సిన obligation వేరుగా ఉంటుంది.

paragraphs.en: A foreign-linked person or entity falling under section 3(2) must secure prior approval from the NBA before the IP right is granted. The 2023 Amendment shifted the trigger from application filing to grant, but it did not replace prior approval with simple registration for this category.
paragraphs.te: Section 3(2) పరిధిలోకి వచ్చే foreign-linked person లేదా entity, IP right grantకు ముందు NBA prior approval తప్పనిసరిగా పొందాలి. 2023 Amendment triggerను application filing నుంచి grantకు మార్చింది. కానీ ఈ categoryకి prior approval స్థానంలో simple registrationను పెట్టలేదు.

paragraphs.en: A section 7 Indian person must complete two distinct steps. Section 6(1A) requires registration with the NBA before the IP right is granted, and section 6(1B) requires NBA prior approval when that right is commercialised. Approval has therefore been deferred to commercialisation, not removed altogether.
paragraphs.te: Section 7 పరిధిలోని Indian person రెండు separate steps complete చేయాలి. Section 6(1A) ప్రకారం IP right grantకు ముందు NBAతో registration చేయాలి. Section 6(1B) ప్రకారం ఆ rightను commercialise చేసే సమయంలో NBA prior approval పొందాలి. అందువల్ల approval remove కాలేదు; commercialisation stageకు defer అయింది.

paragraphs.en: The Amendment replaced the expression 'by-products' with the defined term 'derivative'. A derivative is a naturally occurring biochemical compound produced through the genetic expression or metabolism of biological or genetic resources, whether or not it contains functional units of heredity. This language more closely follows Nagoya Protocol terminology, but the Act and applicable rules must still be applied to decide whether a particular material falls within ABS.
paragraphs.te: Amendment, ‘by-products’ అనే expression స్థానంలో defined term ‘derivative’ను ఉపయోగించింది. Biological లేదా genetic resourcesలో genetic expression లేదా metabolism వల్ల naturally ఏర్పడే biochemical compoundను derivative అంటారు. అందులో functional units of heredity ఉన్నా లేకపోయినా definition వర్తించవచ్చు. ఈ language Nagoya Protocol terminologyకి మరింత దగ్గరగా ఉంది. అయితే particular materialకు ABS వర్తిస్తుందా అనే నిర్ణయం Act, applicable Rules ఆధారంగానే తీసుకోవాలి.

paragraphs.en: The Government describes the 2023 changes as a way to remove unnecessary compliance obstacles affecting research, patenting and AYUSH activity based on Indian biological resources. It points to the later increase in related patent applications as evidence that participation became easier. This is the Government's assessment of policy impact, not a proposition stated in the statutory text.
paragraphs.te: Government వివరణ ప్రకారం 2023 changes, Indian biological resources ఆధారంగా జరిగే research, patenting, AYUSH activityలో unnecessary compliance obstaclesను తగ్గించాయి. తరువాత related patent applications పెరగడాన్ని participation సులభమైందనే evidenceగా Government చూపుతోంది. ఇది statutory textలో ఉన్న proposition కాదు; policy impactపై Government assessment.

paragraphs.en: Critics draw attention to another possible effect. Under the amended arrangement, the NBA has a larger role in negotiating ABS on behalf of local communities, instead of the communities directly helping to settle every benefit-sharing term. Their concern is that simpler compliance may weaken part of the Act's objective of empowering communities.
paragraphs.te: Critics మరో possible effectను గుర్తిస్తున్నారు. ప్రతి benefit-sharing termను settle చేయడంలో local communities directగా పాల్గొనడం బదులు, వారి behalfపై ABS negotiate చేసే NBA role amended arrangementలో పెరిగింది. Compliance సులభమైనా, communitiesను empower చేయాలనే Act objectiveలో ఒక భాగం weaken కావచ్చనేది వారి concern.

paragraphs.en: Supporters and critics are evaluating the same amendment from different policy perspectives. Supporters stress easier compliance, whereas critics stress the possible loss of direct community participation. Neither assessment is the wording of the statute itself. The AYUSH-related exclusion introduced by the amendment remains limited and conditional.
paragraphs.te: Supporters, critics ఒకే Amendmentను different policy perspectives నుంచి evaluate చేస్తున్నారు. Supporters easier complianceను emphasise చేస్తే, critics direct community participation తగ్గే possibilityని emphasise చేస్తున్నారు. ఈ రెండు assessmentsలో ఏదీ statute wording కాదు. Amendment తీసుకొచ్చిన AYUSH-related exclusion limitedగా, conditionsతోనే ఉంటుంది.

paragraphs.en: The AYUSH-related exemption is confined to cultivated medicinal plants and their products where the knowledge used has already been codified in the prescribed authoritative texts. It does not extend to commercial bioprospecting involving wild-harvested resources, cancel the ABS obligations of foreign entities, or remove the NBA from the regulatory system.
paragraphs.te: AYUSH-related exemption, prescribed authoritative textsలో ఇప్పటికే codify అయిన knowledge ఆధారంగా ఉపయోగించే cultivated medicinal plants, వాటి productsకే పరిమితం. Wild-harvested resourcesతో జరిగే commercial bioprospectingకు ఇది వర్తించదు. Foreign entities ABS obligationsను cancel చేయదు; regulatory systemలో NBA roleను కూడా remove చేయదు.

paragraphs.en: The 2023 Amendment did not end benefit sharing. It created only limited, conditional exclusions, while the wider ABS framework continued. That framework includes National, State and Local Biodiversity Funds, each with legally specified receipts and permitted uses.
paragraphs.te: 2023 Amendment benefit sharingను end చేయలేదు. Limited, conditional exclusions మాత్రమే ఇచ్చింది; wider ABS framework కొనసాగుతోంది. ఇందులో National, State, Local Biodiversity Funds ఉంటాయి. ప్రతి Fundలో ఏ receipts చేరాలి, వాటిని ఏ purposesకు use చేయాలి అనేది law చెబుతుంది.

paragraphs.en: The three Biodiversity Funds correspond to the national, state and local levels, but three questions must be answered separately for each fund: which section creates it, which receipts enter it, and what expenditure the Act permits.
paragraphs.te: Three Biodiversity Funds national, State, local levelsకు correspond అవుతాయి. ప్రతి Fund గురించి మూడు questionsను separateగా చూడాలి: ఏ section దాన్ని create చేసింది? ఏ receipts అందులో చేరతాయి? Act ఏ expenditureను permit చేస్తుంది?

paragraphs.en: Section 27 creates the National Biodiversity Fund. It receives section 26 grants and loans, NBA charges and benefit-sharing amounts, and other Central Government-specified sums. It may pay benefit claimers and support conservation, source-area development and locally consulted socio-economic development.
paragraphs.te: Section 27 National Biodiversity Fundను create చేస్తుంది. Section 26 grants and loans, NBA collect చేసే charges, benefit-sharing amounts, Central Government specify చేసే other sums ఇందులో చేరతాయి. Benefit claimersకు payment, conservation, source-area development, local bodiesతో consultation ద్వారా socio-economic developmentకు దీనిని use చేయవచ్చు.

paragraphs.en: Section 32 establishes the State Biodiversity Fund. Its receipts include State grants and loans, NBA allocations and SBB charges or benefit-sharing amounts. It supports conservation, sustainable use, source-area development, BHS management, and compensation or rehabilitation of people economically affected by a BHS notification.
paragraphs.te: Section 32 State Biodiversity Fundను establish చేస్తుంది. State grants and loans, NBA allocations, SBB charges లేదా benefit-sharing amounts ఇందులో చేరతాయి. Conservation, sustainable use, source-area development, BHS management, అలాగే BHS notification వల్ల economically affected peopleకు compensation లేదా rehabilitation కోసం Fundను use చేయవచ్చు.

paragraphs.en: Section 43 creates the Local Biodiversity Fund, and section 44 governs its use. Government or biodiversity-authority grants and loans, section 41(3) BMC access fees and benefit-sharing receipts enter it. Spending must serve biodiversity and the local community within that local body’s jurisdiction.
paragraphs.te: Section 43 Local Biodiversity Fundను create చేస్తుంది; section 44 దాని useను govern చేస్తుంది. Government లేదా biodiversity-authority grants and loans, section 41(3) BMC access fees, benefit-sharing receipts ఇందులో చేరతాయి. Spending ఆ local body jurisdictionలో biodiversity, local community benefitకే ఉండాలి.

paragraphs.en: These Funds show that the BDA controls access and also creates channels for sharing benefits. ABS receipts can move lawfully through national, state and local funds and reach eligible benefit claimers.
paragraphs.te: ఈ Funds వల్ల BDA accessను control చేయడమే కాక benefitsను share చేసే channelsను కూడా create చేస్తుంది. ABS receipts national, State, local Funds ద్వారా legally flow అయి eligible benefit claimersకు చేరవచ్చు.

paragraphs.en: Permitted expenditure becomes progressively more local. The National Fund channels benefits and supports source areas; the State Fund additionally supports BHS management and affected people; the Local Fund is confined to biodiversity and community benefit within its own jurisdiction.
paragraphs.te: National నుంచి local levelకు వచ్చేకొద్దీ permitted expenditure మరింత local-specific అవుతుంది. National Fund benefits, source areasకు support ఇస్తుంది. State Fund BHS management, affected peopleను కూడా cover చేస్తుంది. Local Fund తన jurisdictionలో biodiversity, community benefitకే limited.

paragraphs.en: This pattern reflects subsidiarity: where suitable, decisions and money should be handled close to the resource and community. The same principle connects NBA, SBB and BMC functions, but it creates coordination rather than an administrative command chain.
paragraphs.te: ఈ pattern subsidiarity principleను చూపుతుంది: suitableగా ఉన్నప్పుడు decisions, moneyను resource, communityకు close levelలో handle చేయాలి. ఇదే principle NBA, SBB, BMC functionsను connect చేస్తుంది; కానీ administrative command chainను create చేయదు.

paragraphs.en: Three dates must be separated for the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024: signature on 22 October, Gazette publication on 25 October, and commencement on 24 December 2024 after sixty days. A separate procedural amendment followed on 6 May 2025.
paragraphs.te: Biological Diversity Rules, 2024కు three datesను mix చేయకూడదు: 22 October signature; 25 October Gazette publication; sixty days తరువాత 24 December 2024 commencement. Separate procedural amendment 6 May 2025న వచ్చింది.

paragraphs.en: The Biological Diversity Amendment Rules were separately notified on 6 May 2025. This date is not the signature, publication or commencement date of the principal 2024 Rules. The official Gazette distinguishes the instruments and their G.S.R. notifications.
paragraphs.te: Biological Diversity Amendment Rulesను separateగా 6 May 2025న notify చేశారు. ఈ date principal 2024 Rules signature, publication లేదా commencement date కాదు. Official Gazette instrumentsను, వాటి G.S.R. notificationsను clearly separate చేస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: MoEFCC made the principal Rules under BDA section 62 through G.S.R. 665(E). The instrument was signed on 22 October 2024, but signing alone did not determine commencement because the Rules linked operation to Gazette notification.
paragraphs.te: BDA section 62 powerతో MoEFCC principal Rulesను G.S.R. 665(E)గా చేసింది. Instrument 22 October 2024న sign అయింది. కానీ Rules operationను Gazette notificationతో link చేసినందున signature alone commencementను determine చేయదు.

paragraphs.en: The controlling Gazette is the Gazette of India Extraordinary, Part II, section 3(i), No. 607, with masthead date 25 October 2024 and ID CG-DL-E-25102024-258244. Thus 25 October is the publication date, not 22 October.
paragraphs.te: Controlling Gazette, Gazette of India Extraordinary, Part II, section 3(i), No. 607. Masthead date 25 October 2024; ID CG-DL-E-25102024-258244. కాబట్టి publication date 25 October; 22 October కాదు.

paragraphs.en: Rule 1(2) provides commencement sixty days after Official Gazette notification. Counting from the 25 October 2024 publication gives 24 December 2024 as the commencement date; 22 October remains only the signature date.
paragraphs.te: Rule 1(2) ప్రకారం Official Gazette notification తరువాత sixty daysకు Rules commence అవుతాయి. 25 October 2024 publication నుంచి count చేస్తే commencement 24 December 2024. 22 October signature date మాత్రమే.

paragraphs.en: The apparent three-day discrepancy arises when the 22 October signature date is mistaken for the 25 October publication date. Because the sixty-day period runs from Gazette notification, using the wrong starting date produces the wrong commencement date.
paragraphs.te: 22 October signature dateను 25 October publication dateగా treat చేస్తే three-day discrepancy వస్తుంది. Sixty-day period Gazette notification నుంచి run అవుతుంది; wrong starting date తీసుకుంటే commencement date కూడా wrong అవుతుంది.

paragraphs.en: A rule may be signed and Gazette-published on different dates. When its commencement clause refers to Gazette notification, publication controls the calculation. The BDA and 2023 Amendment provide the statutory framework; the 2024 Rules provide the detailed process from their commencement.
paragraphs.te: Rule signature, Gazette publication different datesలో ఉండవచ్చు. Commencement clause Gazette notificationను refer చేస్తే calculationకు publication dateనే control చేస్తుంది. BDA, 2023 Amendment statutory frameworkను ఇస్తాయి; 2024 Rules commencement నుంచి detailed processను ఇస్తాయి.

paragraphs.en: At national level, the Chennai-based NBA handles section 3(2) access, benefit sharing and other statutory functions. The SBB advises the State Government and handles section 7 prior intimations under sections 23–24. Locally, the BMC prepares and maintains the People’s Biodiversity Register under section 41 and the Rules.
paragraphs.te: National levelలో Chennai-based NBA section 3(2) access, benefit sharing, other statutory functionsను handle చేస్తుంది. SBB State Governmentకు advice ఇచ్చి, sections 23–24 కింద section 7 prior intimationsను deal చేస్తుంది. Local levelలో BMC section 41, Rules ప్రకారం People’s Biodiversity Registerను prepare, maintain చేస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: Do not combine two separate reforms. From 1 April 2024, the 2023 Amendment replaced the relevant BDA imprisonment provisions with monetary adjudication. Amended section 6 also requires a section 3(2) applicant to obtain NBA approval before IP grant rather than before application filing.
paragraphs.te: Two reformsను combine చేయకూడదు. 1 April 2024 నుంచి 2023 Amendment relevant BDA imprisonment provisions స్థానంలో monetary adjudicationను పెట్టింది. Amended section 6 ప్రకారం section 3(2) applicant, IP application filingకు ముందు కాకుండా IP grantకు ముందు NBA approval పొందాలి.

paragraphs.en: A section 7 Indian applicant follows two distinct IP steps: NBA registration before grant under section 6(1A), and NBA prior approval at commercialisation under section 6(1B). Separately, the Amendment provides only specified exclusions connected with cultivated medicinal plants and codified knowledge.
paragraphs.te: Section 7 Indian applicant two IP steps follow చేయాలి: section 6(1A) కింద grantకు ముందు NBA registration; section 6(1B) కింద commercialisation సమయంలో NBA prior approval. దీనికి separateగా cultivated medicinal plants, codified knowledgeకు specified exclusions ఉన్నాయి.

paragraphs.en: The Act creates National, State and Local Biodiversity Funds. The National Fund channels benefits and supports source areas; the State Fund also covers BHS management and affected people; the Local Fund uses receipts, including BMC fees, for biodiversity within its jurisdiction. Purpose becomes more local at each lower level.
paragraphs.te: Act National, State, Local Biodiversity Fundsను create చేస్తుంది. National Fund benefitsను channel చేసి source areasకు support ఇస్తుంది. State Fund BHS management, affected peopleను కూడా cover చేస్తుంది. Local Fund BMC feesతో సహా receiptsను తన jurisdiction biodiversity కోసం use చేస్తుంది. Lower levelకు వెళ్లేకొద్దీ purpose మరింత local అవుతుంది.

paragraphs.en: The BDA framework consists of the NBA, SBBs and local BMCs that maintain PBRs. The 2023 Amendment introduced monetary penalties and limited exclusions. Section 7 applicants register before IP grant and seek approval at commercialisation; section 3(2) applicants need approval before grant. The 2024 Rules were notified as G.S.R. 665(E).
paragraphs.te: BDA frameworkలో NBA, SBBs, PBRలను maintain చేసే local BMCs ఉన్నాయి. 2023 Amendment monetary penalties, limited exclusionsను తీసుకొచ్చింది. Section 7 applicants IP grantకు ముందు register చేసి commercialisationలో approval పొందాలి; section 3(2) applicants grantకు ముందు approval పొందాలి. 2024 Rules G.S.R. 665(E)గా notify అయ్యాయి.

paragraphs.en: G.S.R. 665(E), made under BDA section 62, was signed on 22 October 2024 and published on 25 October in Gazette of India Extraordinary, Part II, section 3(i), No. 607. The publication date controls commencement.
paragraphs.te: BDA section 62 కింద చేసిన G.S.R. 665(E) 22 October 2024న sign అయి, 25 Octoberన Gazette of India Extraordinary, Part II, section 3(i), No. 607లో publish అయింది. Commencementకు publication dateనే controlling date.

paragraphs.en: Rule 1(2) brought the Rules into force sixty days after Gazette notification. Publication on 25 October therefore yields 24 December 2024 as commencement. A separate minor amendment was issued on 6 May 2025.
paragraphs.te: Rule 1(2) ప్రకారం Gazette notification తరువాత sixty daysకు Rules అమల్లోకి వచ్చాయి. 25 October publication ఆధారంగా commencement 24 December 2024. Separate minor amendment 6 May 2025న issue అయింది.

paragraphs.en: Under amended section 37, the State Government may notify a BHS only on an SBB recommendation. Before recommending, the SBB must consult both the relevant local body and BMC. Consultation, recommendation and notification therefore belong to different actors.
paragraphs.te: Amended section 37 ప్రకారం SBB recommendationపై మాత్రమే State Government BHSను notify చేయగలదు. Recommendationకు ముందు SBB relevant local body, BMC రెండింటితో consult చేయాలి. Consultation, recommendation, notification మూడు వేర్వేరు actorsకు చెందిన functions.

paragraphs.en: After the amendment, an SBB recommendation and prior consultation with both the local body and BMC are statutory steps; only the State Government notifies. The September 2026 NBA dashboard figure of 57 BHSs is a dated snapshot, while 44 and the January 2024 WII–ENVIS figure of 54 are older snapshots. A BMC is not subordinate to an SBB.
paragraphs.te: Amendment తరువాత SBB recommendation, local bodyతో పాటు BMC consultation statutory steps; State Government మాత్రమే notify చేస్తుంది. September 2026 NBA dashboardలో 57 BHSs అనేది dated snapshot; 44, January 2024 WII–ENVIS 54 older snapshots. BMC, SBBకు subordinate కాదు.

paragraphs.en: Different authorities constitute the three bodies. The Central Government establishes the NBA under section 8, the State Government establishes the SBB under section 22, and the relevant rural or urban local body constitutes the BMC under section 41(1).
paragraphs.te: Three bodiesను different authorities constitute చేస్తాయి. Section 8 కింద Central Government NBAను, section 22 కింద State Government SBBను, section 41(1) కింద relevant rural లేదా urban local body BMCని constitute చేస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: The institutional pyramid represents coordination and reporting, not command. The September 2026 NBA dashboard listed 2,76,664 BMCs and 2,72,648 PBRs, making this the largest Indian conservation-governance network by institutional count. The totals indicate reach, not the quality of every register.
paragraphs.te: Institutional pyramid coordination, reportingను చూపుతుంది; commandను కాదు. September 2026 NBA dashboardలో 2,76,664 BMCs, 2,72,648 PBRs ఉన్నాయి. Institutional count ప్రకారం ఇది Indiaలో largest conservation-governance network. Totals reachను చూపుతాయి; every register qualityని కాదు.

paragraphs.en: Turmeric wound-healing, neem pesticidal and basmati name or trait claims became major biopiracy disputes before India had a domestic ABS law. India challenged them through legal and diplomatic routes. India ratified the CBD in 1994 and enacted the BDA in 2002; the 1990s disputes increased the political urgency for legislation.
paragraphs.te: Turmeric wound-healing, neem pesticidal, basmati name లేదా trait claims domestic ABS lawకు ముందు major biopiracy disputes అయ్యాయి. India వాటిని legal, diplomatic routesలో challenge చేసింది. India 1994లో CBD ratify చేసి, 2002లో BDA enact చేసింది; 1990s disputes legislation urgencyని పెంచాయి.

paragraphs.en: Benefit sharing was not abolished by the 2023 Amendment. It introduced only specified exclusions associated with cultivated medicinal plants, codified traditional knowledge and eligible actors. Foreign-linked ABS duties and the NBA’s broader statutory role continue.
paragraphs.te: 2023 Amendment benefit sharingను abolish చేయలేదు. Cultivated medicinal plants, codified traditional knowledge, eligible actorsకు సంబంధించిన specified exclusions మాత్రమే ఇచ్చింది. Foreign-linked ABS duties, NBA broader statutory role కొనసాగుతాయి.

paragraphs.en: The move from IP filing to grant was not confined to Indian applicants. Substituted section 6 uses grant as the relevant stage for both Indian and foreign-linked applicants; the difference lies in whether registration or prior approval is required and when commercialisation approval applies.
paragraphs.te: IP filing నుంచి grantకు shift Indian applicantsకే limited కాదు. Substituted section 6లో Indian, foreign-linked applicants ఇద్దరికీ grant relevant stage. Difference registrationనా, prior approvalనా, commercialisation approval ఎప్పుడు అవసరమా అన్న obligationలో ఉంటుంది.

paragraphs.en: Section 3(2) applicants require NBA prior approval before grant under section 6(1). Section 7 Indian applicants register before grant under section 6(1A) and obtain prior approval at commercialisation under section 6(1B). This second step means the Indian route is not approval-free.
paragraphs.te: Section 3(2) applicants section 6(1) కింద grantకు ముందు NBA prior approval పొందాలి. Section 7 Indian applicants section 6(1A) కింద grantకు ముందు register చేసి, section 6(1B) కింద commercialisationలో prior approval పొందాలి. ఈ second step వల్ల Indian route approval-free కాదు.

paragraphs.en: An Indian section 7 applicant is not wholly exempt from NBA approval. Section 6(1A) requires registration before grant, while section 6(1B) still requires prior approval when the resulting IP right is commercialised.
paragraphs.te: Indian section 7 applicantకు NBA approval నుంచి complete exemption లేదు. Section 6(1A) grantకు ముందు registration కోరుతుంది; resulting IP right commercialise చేసే సమయంలో section 6(1B) prior approval ఇంకా అవసరం.

paragraphs.en: For section 7 applicants, section 6(1B) postpones approval to commercialisation; it does not remove it. Do not confuse this IP rule with BHS procedure: under section 37 the SBB recommends after consultation, and only the State Government notifies.
paragraphs.te: Section 7 applicantsకు section 6(1B) approvalను commercialisation వరకు postpone చేస్తుంది; remove చేయదు. ఈ IP ruleను BHS procedureతో mix చేయకూడదు. Section 37 కింద consultation తరువాత SBB recommend చేస్తుంది; State Government మాత్రమే notify చేస్తుంది.

paragraphs.en: The State Government cannot bypass amended section 37(1). The SBB must first consult the relevant local body and BMC and then recommend the site; only afterwards may the State Government notify it. The legal order is consultation, recommendation, notification.
paragraphs.te: State Government amended section 37(1)ను bypass చేయలేదు. SBB ముందుగా relevant local body, BMCతో consult చేసి siteను recommend చేయాలి; తరువాత మాత్రమే State Government notify చేయగలదు. Legal order: consultation, recommendation, notification.

paragraphs.en: The claim that a BMC has no formal section 37 role relies on the old provision. The substituted section expressly requires consultation with both the local body and BMC before an SBB recommends a BHS. Omitting BMC consultation now omits a statutory step.
paragraphs.te: BMCకు section 37లో formal role లేదనే claim old provisionపై ఆధారపడింది. Substituted section ప్రకారం SBB BHS recommend చేయడానికి ముందు local body, BMC రెండింటితో expressly consult చేయాలి. BMC consultation omit చేస్తే statutory step miss అవుతుంది.

paragraphs.en: BMCs are not village field units of an SBB. Section 8 assigns NBA establishment to the Central Government, section 22 assigns SBB establishment to the State Government, and section 41(1) assigns BMC constitution to the local body.
paragraphs.te: BMCs, SBB village field units కావు. Section 8 NBA establishmentను Central Governmentకు, section 22 SBB establishmentను State Governmentకు, section 41(1) BMC constitutionను local bodyకి assign చేస్తాయి.

paragraphs.en: A BMC is locally constituted and is not subordinate to an SBB; the three levels coordinate without forming a command chain. The Act also creates National, State and Local Biodiversity Funds. Charges, royalties and benefit-sharing receipts enter the relevant funds and finance legally assigned purposes so benefits can reach eligible claimers.
paragraphs.te: BMC localగా constitute అవుతుంది; SBBకు subordinate కాదు. Three levels command chainగా కాక coordinationతో పనిచేస్తాయి. Act National, State, Local Biodiversity Fundsను కూడా create చేస్తుంది. Charges, royalties, benefit-sharing receipts relevant Fundsలో చేరి legally assigned purposesకు finance ఇస్తాయి; benefits eligible claimersకు చేరేలా చేస్తాయి.
